title: A Autopsy for the Inheritance
premise: Cyrus Montrose, the cathedral's reclusive archivist, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after wealthy benefactor Edmund Vale's funeral—claiming Edmund was murdered and naming the locked crypt as the hiding place of proof. As Cyrus decodes a ledger concealed in the cathedral's memorial plaques, he uncovers a network of stolen identities: Edmund himself was a fraud, and several prominent townspeople, including Cyrus's own late mentor, were living under assumed names. When the killer begins destroying the ledger's entries to protect their own buried past, Cyrus must choose between exposing everyone's secrets—including his own forged credentials—and letting a murder go unpunished. In the end, Cyrus traps the killer in the crypt with the ledger's final cipher, then quietly burns the pages that would ruin the innocent, finding justice outside the law and, for the first time, a place he truly belongs.
about_author: Sable Yarrow is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of births, deaths, and disappearances in English cathedral towns. Their fiction is drawn to quiet people who keep other people's secrets—and to the moment those secrets refuse to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Day After the Funeral
chapters.summary: Cyrus Montrose, POV. Three days after Edmund Vale's grand funeral, Cyrus sorts condolence mail in the archive and finds a confession letter claiming Vale was murdered, postmarked the day after the burial. The letter names the locked crypt. Emotional beat: dread breaking through Cyrus's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: A Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Searching Vale's donated papers, Cyrus notices the memorial plaque inscriptions form a numeric sequence—a ledger keyed to the cathedral's stones. The crypt key has been recut recently. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into fear that the writer is watching him.

chapters.title: The Widow's Gratitude
chapters.summary: Vera Vale, POV. The widow thanks the cathedral staff, probing Cyrus about her husband's papers with questions too precise for grief. She mentions a letter Edmund never received. Emotional beat: Cyrus realizes someone in the family may already be searching—and may be dangerous.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Using a borrowed key, Cyrus enters the crypt at night and finds Vale's private strongbox: a second ledger, photographs, and a list of names, each annotated with a date and the words 'paid in full.' Emotional beat: vertigo—his quiet world is built on other people's buried lives.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Detective Inspector Ruth Okonkwo, POV. Okonkwo, dissatisfied with Vale's official cause of death, interviews the household and notes the archivist's nervousness. Emotional beat: her dogged decency contrasts with Cyrus's secrecy; the law and Cyrus begin circling the same truth.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Deciphering the ledger, Cyrus finds his dead mentor, Canon Aldous, listed under a name that wasn't his—along with a payment. The confession letter's handwriting, Cyrus realizes, resembles Aldous's. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal; the one person he trusted was part of Vale's web.

chapters.title: Everyone Was Someone Else
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cross-referencing parish records, Cyrus maps the pattern: Vale sold new identities to people fleeing their old ones. Half the cathedral's benefactors are on the list. Emotional beat: a terrible kinship—Cyrus's own forged credentials mean he is one of them.

chapters.title: A Fire in the Records Room
chapters.summary: Okonkwo, POV. A small fire damages the parish registry the night after Cyrus's visit; someone is erasing paper trails. Okonkwo suspects the archivist. Emotional beat: rising stakes—the killer is ahead of them, and Cyrus is now a suspect.

chapters.title: The Confession's Second Page
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. A second letter arrives, warning Cyrus to stop, written in the same disguised hand. Forensic comparison suggests the writer learned penmanship from Aldous—meaning the confessor is a former protégé, someone from Cyrus's own lost years. Emotional beat: hunted by a ghost of his past.

chapters.title: Vera's Second Mourning
chapters.summary: Vera Vale, POV. Vera privately confronts Cyrus, revealing she knew her husband's trade and married him inside it—her own name was bought too. She begs him to let the dead stay dead. Emotional beat: complicity and loneliness; belonging purchased at the price of truth.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Silence
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The old sexton, Tom Brack, who holds the crypt's true original key, is found unconscious on the crypt steps. Cyrus realizes the confessor is inside the cathedral's inner circle. Emotional beat: paranoia; no face is safe to trust.

chapters.title: Entries Missing
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Comparing the crypt ledger against the plaque cipher, Cyrus finds four entries physically cut from the strongbox ledger—someone has already claimed them. One missing name matches a man who died mysteriously a decade ago. Emotional beat: the killer's motive sharpens—survival, not greed.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Cold Case
chapters.summary: Okonkwo, POV. Digging into the decade-old death, Okonkwo finds the 'dead' man may have assumed a new identity—and may still live in town under a respected name. Emotional beat: the case widens; the murderer may be a pillar of the community.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Buried
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. A flashback chapter: how Cyrus bought his own name from Vale's network after fleeing a scandal, and how Aldous sponsored him. He understands now why Aldous kept the ledger—and why Aldous died conveniently before it could surface. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. The confessor proposes a meeting: bring the ledger, or the next fire takes the archive—and Cyrus's own forged papers with it. Cyrus notices the letter's paper stock matches stationery from the Vale house. Emotional beat: cornered, but finally holding a thread that leads somewhere.

chapters.title: Among the Benefactors
chapters.summary: Okonkwo and Cyrus, POV alternating. Forced into wary alliance, they narrow the suspects to three: Vale's lawyer, the cathedral's head verger, and Vera's brother. Each has a ledger-adjacent past. Emotional beat: grudging trust; two keepers of secrets working by candlelight.

chapters.title: The Verger's Hands
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus baits each suspect with a false ledger detail; only the head verger, Marcus Fell, reacts—correcting an error only the ledger's true reader could catch. Emotional beat: cold confirmation; the man who greets every parishioner by name knows everyone's real name too.

chapters.title: Why Fell Killed
chapters.summary: Okonkwo, POV. Okonkwo traces Fell's history: he was the 'dead' man from a decade ago, and Vale was blackmailing him anew. Aldous had discovered Fell's cuts from the ledger and was about to tell. Emotional beat: the murderer is not a monster but a man defending a life he built from nothing—Cyrus's dark mirror.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Cyrus lets Fell believe the ledger's final cipher reveals a hidden payment vault, luring him to the crypt at night. Fell comes to burn the last pages and silence Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror and strange calm—Cyrus choosing, for once, to stand in the light.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Okonkwo and Cyrus, POV. Okonkwo takes Fell in the crypt as he confesses to Cyrus; the locked door, meant as a trap, nearly becomes a tomb for both when Fell panics. Emotional beat: the climax—violence, near-drowning among the coffins, and Fell's broken admission that he only wanted to belong.

chapters.title: What the Law Can't Touch
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Fell is charged with murder, but the ledger would destroy dozens of innocent lives built on bought names. Cyrus testifies only to what convicts Fell, then burns the ledger's remaining pages before Okonkwo's eyes—and she chooses to look away. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, and the weight of that choice.

chapters.title: A Name He Chose
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Weeks later, Vera donates her husband's estate to the archive; Cyrus is formally offered the post of cathedral historiographer—his real name on the contract at last, whatever his history. He writes his own entry in the new ledger. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—belonging not bought, but given and accepted.
